newsitem.title: USA: Northrop to cut 1,100 workers, take $90 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Northrop to cut 1,100 workers, take $90 million charge.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp. said Wednesday it will close four plants and cut at least 1,100 jobs, resulting in a pretax $90 million restructuring charge in the fourth quarter.

The nation's fifth-largest defence contractor said the moves were meant to streamline operations and keep it competitive as aerospace companies fight for a shrinking number of orders for military gear.
The job cuts amount to 2.4 percent of the 46,600 work force at Los Angeles-based Northrop. The company also said it was hiring at some plants, reducing the net job losses to 755.

"We regret that these actions will result in the loss of jobs, but they are necessary if we are to meet the affordability demands of our customers and win new business," Chairman Kent Kresa said in a statement.
The brunt of the cuts will be felt in California, New York and Florida. The plants to be closed are in Hawthorne, Calif., Great River on Long Island, N.Y., Stuart, Fla., and Perry, Ga.

The Hawthorne plant, which makes electronic sensors, navigation and guidance systems and anti-tank weapons, will close by year-end and most production will be transferred to plants in Rolling Meadows, Ill., and Benton Park, Pa.
The plant has 770 employees and about 240 will be offered transfers, Northrop said.

The Great River plant, which makes electronic test and targeting equipment, will be closed by mid-year, the company said, and 120 of its 450 workers will be offered transfers. Northrop's three other plants on Long Island were unaffected.
In Stuart, Fla., about half of the work force of 500 will loose their jobs and the rest offered transfers. The plant, which makes aircraft parts, will close at the end of 1998.

In addition, more jobs may be cut at the Perry, Ga., facility, which will close within two years. Current plans are to transfer the plant's 450 workers to another Georgia plant if the company wins new commercial contracts. A decision is expected by mid-year.
The company said it will add jobs at plants in Texas, Georgia, Illinois and Pennsylvania.
The $90 million pretax charge includes $60 million for closing the plants and $30 million related to the job cuts and other one-time costs, it said.
Northrop stock fell 50 cents to $77.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
